newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian leader thanks U.S. for MFN status.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian leader thanks U.S. for MFN status.

text.p: Cambodian leader Prince Norodom Ranariddh thanked the United States on Thursday for granting the country Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trading privileges, a U.S. diplomat said.
First Prime Minister Ranariddh conveyed his thanks at a ceremony marking the inauguration of a U.S.-funded bridge on a key highway linking Phnom Penh to the northwest.
"He profusedly thanked the United States for the bridge and MFN," said the diplomat.
President Bill Clinton on Wednesday signed a bill granting Cambodia MFN status, declaring it would aid efforts to establish democracy and economic reforms in the country.
MFN cuts taxes on hundreds of exports and enables countries to compete better in trade with the United States. It also expands opportunities for U.S. business and investment.
